problem: The requested reuse of page data is unsupported by the current restricted Studio language. Changing the prompt alone cannot implement it.

options.name: Explicit capture and separate run-local references
options.tradeoff: Adds bounded capture/read operations and cross-step validation while preserving immutable input variables.

options.name: Mutable input vars
options.tradeoff: Conflates declared inputs with browser-derived values and complicates reference, vault, and redaction semantics.

options.name: General JavaScript assignments
options.tradeoff: Widens the restricted execution language and requires expression and scope semantics beyond this use case.

proposedFlow: Plain English producer and consumer steps
Versioned compile prompt proposes restricted capture/reference syntax
Validator lowers accepted syntax to typed operations and validates ordered dependencies
Executor creates a fresh run-local capture map
Browser adapter reads text at the producer step
Later fill/assert operations resolve the captured value
Existing step results and recording show the flow
constraints: Generated JavaScript remains unexecuted; only typed operations execute.
Captured values never enter compilation, persisted artifacts, input declarations, or vault references.
A capture map belongs to one execution and starts empty.
Reject duplicate definitions, forward reads, missing producers, and forbidden reference positions.
Validate the complete assembled artifact after incremental edits.
Define visible text, whitespace, empty value, strict locator, and timeout behavior explicitly before implementation.
Configure limits for capture names, count, and value bytes.
Extend redaction to newly captured values before a later failure can disclose them.
Keep navigation and secret-input semantics unchanged.
versioning: Coordinate validator, executor, syntax-reference and prompt pins and fixtures; use existing compatibility gates to require recompilation. Evaluate envelope change only if JSON shape changes.
acceptance: Create and run through Studio using a declared base URL/input variable alongside captured data.
A local fixture generates an unpredictable value only when the runner requests the source page.
Capture that value, navigate to a later page, fill a field, and submit.
The fixture independently compares submitted and issued values and records a receipt.
Run twice without recompiling: identical confirmed revision and artifact hash, different issued values, matching receipts.
Neither generated value may appear in authored steps, declared inputs, or compiled literals.
Concurrent and consecutive runs cannot share captures.
Missing targets, ambiguous targets, absent producers, duplicate captures, forward reads, oversized values and cancellation fail predictably; dependent steps do not execute after failure.
Capture values are absent from diagnostics, events and manifests; recordings remain governed by existing evidence behavior.
Review step results and logs; play recordings and seek to producer/consumer offsets.
Run targeted runner/backend tests, real Chromium fixtures, compatibility and reference drift tests, then repeat the live Studio acceptance flow.
